files.lesson.md: --- order: 12 unit: reals9 node: AC9M9N01 n3 uses: [AC9M9N01 n1, AC9M9N01 n2] assumes: [AC9M8N01 n1, AC9M8N01 n2] connection: part-tolerance title: Ranges on the line summary: "A tolerance or a safe range is a stretch of the number line. ≤ and ≥ include the end (a closed circle); < and > leave it out (an open circle)." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A hole has to be 20 mm, give or take a tiny bit. Where's the line between a part that fits and one that doesn't?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8350 url: http://127.0.0.1:8350/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- Real numbers fill the whole number line, so a range is a stretch of it with two ends. The ends need care. ## Predict: does it pass? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to pass or fail for a hole at 20.04 mm shows who reads the tolerance as a single number and who sees the range." check: type: predict q: "A bolt hole must be 20 mm, give or take 0.05 mm. A hole is measured at 20.04 mm. Does it pass?" options: - "Yes: it's inside the range" - "No: it isn't 20 mm" - "No: it's more than 20 mm" - "You can't tell without a bigger ruler" actual: "Yes. The range is from 20 − 0.05 = 19.95 mm to 20 + 0.05 = 20.05 mm. 20.04 is between them, so it passes." ``` The drawing says 20 mm, give or take 0.05 mm. The measured hole is 20.04 mm. Does it pass? ## Run: mark the limits ```step stage: run insight: "Marking both limits on the line shows the passing range as a stretch with two ends, and the measured hole sits inside it." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Drag A to the smallest hole that passes (19.95) and B to the biggest (20.05). Is the measured hole between them? Was your prediction right?", when: "x(A) = 19.95 and x(B) = 20.05" } ``` The measured hole is the fixed point. Drag $A$ and $B$ to the two limits. ## Investigate: closed and open ends ```step stage: investigate insight: "A range with its end points included uses ≤ and ≥ (closed circles); leaving them out uses < and > (open circles). Ben's strict signs would fail a hole of exactly 20.05." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Which inequality describes every hole that passes, from 19.95 mm to 20.05 mm, including both limits?" options: ["$19.95 \\le x \\le 20.05$", "$19.95 < x < 20.05$", "$x \\le 20.05$", "$x = 20$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That leaves out holes of exactly 19.95 and 20.05, which still pass.", "That lets in holes much too small.", "That means only exactly 20 mm."] explain: "≤ keeps the end points: a closed circle at each limit." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ben" text: "Ben writes the passing range. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: interval-ends-open explain: "Line 2: < leaves the ends out, but a hole of exactly 19.95 or 20.05 passes. It should be 19.95 ≤ x ≤ 20.05." - check: type: number q: "A shaft must be $12$ mm, give or take $0.02$ mm. What's the smallest length that passes?" answer: 11.98 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "12 − 0.02 = 11.98 mm." ``` ### Both limits Here's turning a tolerance into a range on the line. ```worked 20 \pm 0.05 :: The drawing: 20 mm, give or take 0.05. 20 - 0.05 = 19.95 :: The lower limit. 20 + 0.05 = 20.05 :: The upper limit. 19.95 \le x \le 20.05 :: Both ends count: closed circles. 20.04 \text{ is between } 19.95 \text{ and } 20.05 :: So it passes. ``` Now try one on paper: a shaft of 12 mm ± 0.02 mm. Write the range, then type the upper limit. ### Find the mistake Read Ben's working. Which signs keep the end? ### How small? ## Modify: change the ends ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing one end at a time: a ray from one number, closed or open, then a range and the whole numbers in it." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#vary", height: 560 } tasks: - hint: ["Drag P to 2.", "x ≥ 2 includes 2: a closed circle, pointing right."] check: { type: board, text: "Set the board to $x \\ge 2$: a closed circle at 2, with the line going right.", when: "x(P) = 2 and k = 1 and s = 1" } - hint: ["List them: 3, 4, …", "x < 8 leaves 8 out."] check: { type: number, q: "How many whole numbers satisfy $3 \\le x < 8$?", answer: 5, explain: "3, 4, 5, 6, 7: five. 8 is left out." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Which is the biggest whole number with $x < 8$?", answer: 7, explain: "8 isn't allowed because the sign is <, so 7 is the biggest." } - hint: ["√2 is 1.4142…", "Is that between 1.41 and 1.42?"] check: { type: question, q: "Edge case: is $\\sqrt{2}$ in the range $1.41 \\le x \\le 1.42$?", options: ["Yes: √2 = 1.4142…", "No: √2 isn't a number you can place", "No: it's not equal to 1.41 or 1.42"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Every real number has a place on the line, even if it never ends.", "It doesn't have to equal an end: it just has to be between them."], explain: "1.41 ≤ 1.4142… ≤ 1.42." } ``` ### A ray ### Whole numbers in a range ### An irrational in a range ## Practise: read and write ranges ```step stage: practise insight: "Writing and reading ranges with open and closed ends, mixed; the review keeps exact and rounded values separate." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A part must be $50$ mm ± $0.1$ mm. What's the upper limit?" answer: 50.1 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "50 + 0.1 = 50.1 mm." - check: type: question q: "Which means 'at least 5, but less than 9'?" options: ["$5 \\le x < 9$", "$5 < x \\le 9$", "$5 \\le x \\le 9$", "$5 < x < 9$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That leaves out 5 but keeps 9.", "That keeps 9: it says 'less than 9'.", "That leaves out 5: it says 'at least 5'."] explain: "At least 5 includes 5 (≤). Less than 9 leaves out 9 (<)." smaller: check: { type: "question", q: "'At least 5' includes 5. Which sign keeps the end?", options: ["≤", "<"], answer: 0, explain: "≤ and ≥ keep the end point." } - check: type: number q: "Three holes are measured: $19.94$, $20.03$ and $20.05$ mm. How many pass the range $19.95 \\le x \\le 20.05$?" answer: 2 explain: "19.94 is below 19.95: fails. 20.03 and 20.05 pass." - check: type: question q: "Review: which is exact?" options: ["$\\sqrt{3}$", "$1.73$", "$1.732$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "1.73 is rounded.", "1.732 is rounded."] explain: "√3 is exact; each decimal is a rounded version." ``` ### Tolerance ### Which signs ### How many pass ### Review Exact or rounded, from the last lesson. ## Make: back to the bolt hole ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the opening: the range, the measurement and the decision, with the ends handled correctly." tasks: - hint: ["Lower and upper limits first.", "Then check each measurement against both ends."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The drawing says 20 mm ± 0.05 mm. Four holes measure 19.95, 20.00, 20.06 and 19.99 mm. How many pass?" steps: - ["$19.95 \\le x \\le 20.05$", "lower limit 19.95, upper limit 20.05, both included"] - ["19.95 ✓, 20.00 ✓, 19.99 ✓", "inside the range, 19.95 sits on the lower end"] - ["20.06 ✗", "bigger than 20.05"] answer: "3" answerLabel: "Holes that pass" feedback: - ["2", "19.95 is on the end and the end counts: ≤."] - ["4", "20.06 is more than 20.05: it fails."] criteria: - "I wrote both limits before checking any hole." - "I counted the hole on the end as a pass." - "I checked each hole against both ends." explain: "19.95, 20.00 and 19.99 pass; 20.06 is too big." - check: type: question q: "A sign says 'height under 4.0 m'. Does a truck of exactly 4.0 m fit?" options: ["No: under 4.0 leaves out 4.0", "Yes: 4.0 is the limit", "Only if it's a small truck"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "'Under' means less than, which leaves out the end.", "The size doesn't matter: the height is exactly 4.0."] explain: "x < 4.0: an open circle at 4.0." ``` ### Which pass? Back to the bolt hole. Work it out on paper first, then type your answer. ### An open end The hole sizes and the drawing here are made up for the task. **Also used in** - **Making things.** Every machined part has a tolerance range on its drawing. - **Next lesson.** Using exact and rounded real numbers in formulas, including π. ```teacher summary: Students turn a tolerance into a range on the number line, use ≤ and < to keep or leave out the ends, and check measurements against it (AC9M9N01, node 3). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can write a tolerance as a range with its limits. - I can show a range on the number line with open and closed ends. - I can decide if a measurement is in a range. struggle: "Open or closed ends. Ask: does the end point itself count?" before: > Students need Exact or rounded?. The one idea: a range has two ends, and each end is in or out. The common mistake is leaving both out when the limits count (Ben's working). The bolt hole, shaft and measurements are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose 'No: it isn't 20 mm' read the tolerance as one number." - "Run: ask students to say each limit before dragging." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the four holes in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for both limits written first." - "Modify: before 3 ≤ x < 8, ask whether 8 is in." stuck: - see: A student fails a hole of exactly 19.95. ask: Is the limit itself allowed? fix: "Yes: ≤ keeps the end. It passes." - see: A student writes the range as 20 < x < 0.05. ask: What are the two limits as numbers? fix: 19.95 and 20.05. stretch: A measuring tool reads to 0.01. What's the biggest real hole that could read 20.05? support: A number line from 19.9 to 20.1 with the limits already marked. leads: | Continues AC9M9N01 node 3. Where it leads: absolute and relative error (Year 9), solving inequalities. exit: q: A part is 30 mm ± 0.2 mm. Write the range. a: 29.8 ≤ x ≤ 30.2. explain: > A tolerance gives a range on the number line: 20 ± 0.05 means $19.95 \le x \le 20.05$. ≤ and ≥ keep the end (a closed circle). < and > leave it out (an open circle). ```
files.line.yml:
# Number lines for "Ranges on the line". Tolerance limits for a bolt hole, then rays.

# region: run
widget: numberline
range: 19.9, 20.1
labels: 0.05
snap: 0.01
point M: 20.04, Measured hole
point A: 19.9, drag
point B: 20.1, drag
compare: A, B
# endregion

# region: vary
widget: numberline
range: -2, 10
snap: 1
point P: 0, drag
ray: P
# endregion
files.working.txt:
# Ben's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: ben
A hole passes if it is from 19.95 mm up to 20.05 mm, including both limits.
So 19.95 < x < 20.05.
A hole of exactly 20.05 mm passes.
# endregion
